title: Scott Wolter Claims New Evidence Shows Location of Atlantis Off Portugal

content:
​Former America Unearthed host Scott F. Wolter appeared on Randall Carlson’s podcast yesterday to share what he claims is new evidence for Atlantis around 38°N and 9°W, just off the coast of Portugal near Cape St. Vincent. Wolter said that a British man named Hamilton White contacted him to share the artifacts, which he were associated with Atlantis and had been dredged up off the coast of Portugal. Wolter also said that the CIA and Mossad intervened to warn White against sharing the material with Wolter, whom they allegedly said was not credible. However, the ill-prepared Wolter had only just received an envelope of White’s photographs and rushed to Carlson’s podcast without having made any effort to evaluate them, so most of the ninety-minute program involved the two men saying they did not understand what they were looking at. 

​The artifacts were not terribly impressive. One, which looked like a slab of rock, White described as a “Baghdad battery,” though it contained neither the clay vessel nor the copper and iron rods seen in the original, discovered in 1936. The stone had a shallow cylindrical hole drilled into one side. Wolter showed some other rocks that also had holes drilled into them, which Carlson and Wolter conceded looked more like slag than Atlantean technology, though Wolter argued that bits on the rocks were “welded” to them.

The alleged "battery" shown to Scott Wolter.

​Wolter then showed a photograph of black splotches, which left Carlson quite confused. Wolter seemingly expected his audience to gasp in awe, though even he seemingly couldn’t remember what the picture was supposed to be. He read the 2010 copyright date off the image and its attribution to the U.S. Navy. “Uh okay. I'm just going to keep going here,” he said after Carlson asked him what he was supposed to see in it. Wolter then showed a drawing White made of the splotches in which White had depicted them as the floor plans of irregular buildings, and Wolter took the drawing for evidence that the photo in fact depicted an image of the sunken ruins of Atlantis.

 Wolter showed a number of other images, ranging from blurry photographs of reflections or shadows in water to unexplained drawings

 “I don’t know. I’m frankly a little confused,” Wolter said.

 He also showed documents in Portuguese, one of which stated that it was a survey of the west coast of Portugal along the capes of Roca and Sines. Carlson asked what the document was. “I have no idea,” Wolter replied.

 Based on this material, the two men discussed whether a raised underwater feature off the coast of Portugal might be the sunken Atlantis. They then speculated on the relationship between the continental shelf off Portugal and the Azores, another place often claimed as a remnant of Atlantis. The two agreed that Atlantis was probably land on the continental shelf beyond Portugal during the Ice Age, when sea levels were lower, with colonies spread around other high ground in the Atlantic, such as the Azores. “Maybe there’s going to be connections that we find if we’re able to dig deeper or dive deeper into the site that we're looking at here that Hamilton shared with us,” Wolter said. “Maybe there will be a connection made to the Azores. Who knows?”
